youtube.title: Rust Day 5: Constants & Shadowing Explained 🦀 #Shorts

scenes.say: Rust, day five. Constants, and shadowing: same name, brand new value.

scenes.heading: Constants
scenes.say: Constants use const, not let. They're always immutable, so no mut, and the type is required, here u32. Names are all caps, and constants can live outside functions.
scenes.captions: Constants use const, not let. They're always immutable, so no mut, and the type is required, here u32. Names are all caps, and constants can live outside functions.

scenes.heading: const vs let
scenes.say: Use constants for shared values, like a maximum score. Their value must be known at compile time.

scenes.heading: Shadowing

steps.at: let x equals x plus one

scenes.say: Now shadowing. let x equals five. let x equals x plus one makes a brand new x: six. Inside the braces, another x shadows it: twelve. After the block, x is six again.
scenes.captions: Now shadowing. let x = 5. let x = x + 1 makes a brand new x: 6. Inside the braces, another x shadows it: 12. After the block, x is 6 again.

scenes.heading: Run it
scenes.caption: inner 12, outer 6
scenes.say: Run it: twelve inside the block, six outside. Exactly as traced.

scenes.heading: Each let = a new x
scenes.say: Each let stacks a new variable. The old one is hidden, not changed.

scenes.heading: Common mistake
scenes.say: Shadowing can even change the type. But with mut, putting a number into a text variable fails.

scenes.heading: The real error
scenes.caption: E0308: mismatched types
scenes.say: Error E0308, mismatched types: expected a string slice, found a number. Shadow it with let instead.
scenes.captions: Error E0308, mismatched types: expected a &str, found a number. Shadow it with let instead.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.say: Recap: constants are always immutable and need a type. Shadowing makes a new variable and can change its type. mut can't.
